Synopsis:
                    Climate warming is driving a structural shift in boreal forests from evergreen-dominant (spruce, fir) to deciduous-dominant tree cover. Post-disturbance recovery (wildfires, storms), extended growing seasons and increased soil nitrogen all favour deciduous species. Observational data from Alaska and Canada confirm early-stage transition. The shift carries implications for carbon, water and energy cycles at scale.
